items.title: Retriever-Free Retrieval: Navigating Documents with Decision Models
items.summary: DecisionRAG uses pretrained language models as decision models to improve document retrieval beyond lexical matching.
items.whyItMatters: It could reduce retrieval bottlenecks, enabling more accurate AI responses for tech professionals.

items.title: Center-of-Mass Interpretation of Evolution Strategies
items.summary: The article explains evolution strategies as a center-of-mass update, treating perturbed models as particles weighted by reward, offering a geometric view of the algorithm.
items.whyItMatters: It provides a clearer intuition for ES, aiding developers to debug and improve gradient-free optimization methods.

items.title: Auto-Research Arena: Benchmarking and Advancing Auto-Research in Language Modeling
items.summary: Auto-Research Arena is a benchmark that evaluates autonomous research systems and helps discover new ideas in language modeling.
items.whyItMatters: It enables systematic progress and comparison of AI research automation, crucial for advancing language model innovation.

items.title: Learning Force-Reactive Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
items.summary: The article introduces FLORE, a framework that learns force-reactive humanoid locomotion and manipulation using robot-free demonstrations with force-sensing handhelds.
items.whyItMatters: It enables more natural, safe human‑robot interactions by coordinating force and motion across a humanoid’s body.

items.title: On the stability of learning
items.summary: The paper examines how learning algorithms perform when gradient signals are sparse, local, and intermittently noisy, as in biological neural networks.
items.whyItMatters: It informs design of robust AI systems that can learn under realistic, imperfect feedback conditions.

items.title: Patient-specific rubric-based evaluation of large language models across longitudinal cancer care
items.summary: NPC-RubricBench evaluates LLMs on multistage reasoning throughout nasopharyngeal carcinoma care, not just single encounters.
items.whyItMatters: It tests AI’s real‑world clinical continuity, crucial for reliable oncology support.

items.title: Preserve to Expand: Source-Aware Adaptation and Model Merging for Multilingual LLM-Based ASR
items.summary: The paper explores methods to add new languages to multilingual speech‑to‑text systems without losing existing language performance, focusing on connector‑based LLMs.
items.whyItMatters: Tech‑savvy readers care because it enables scalable, privacy‑preserving multilingual ASR upgrades.

items.title: Work Agents: Systems, Capabilities, and Optimization
items.summary: The article discusses how evolving foundation models enable work agents to perform complex tasks across tools and workflows, proposing a unified system-level view to improve reliability.
items.whyItMatters: It offers a framework for building more dependable AI agents that can automate real-world work tasks efficiently.

items.title: I-HITL: Inalienable Human-in-the-Loop
items.summary: The article proposes an inalienable human‑in‑the‑loop (I‑HITL) protocol to guarantee AI agents cannot bypass human approval for critical actions.
items.whyItMatters: It offers a stronger safety mechanism for AI systems that could impact high‑stakes decisions.

items.title: Information-Theoretic Secure Aggregation With Heterogeneous Client Quantization
items.summary: The paper proposes a secure aggregation scheme for federated learning that accommodates clients using different quantization levels due to bandwidth constraints.
items.whyItMatters: It improves privacy and efficiency for diverse edge devices in federated learning.

items.title: Profiling a Frontier Agent with EBench: From Direct Control to Harness with Policy
items.summary: The report evaluates GPT‑6‑Astra as a core agent on EBench, comparing its direct control of robots to post‑trained VLA and WAM policies across manipulation tasks.
items.whyItMatters: It shows how frontier multimodal LLMs can replace specialized training, impacting robotics automation and AI integration.

items.title: Reva: Real-Time Vulnerability Detection through Contextual Probing of Large Language Models
items.summary: Reva uses large language models to detect software vulnerabilities in real time by probing code context and running analysis tools.
items.whyItMatters: It helps developers catch costly bugs early, improving security and reducing remediation effort.

items.title: Understanding Jev-Style System One Models: Does Structure Reduce Selection Bias?
items.summary: Selection bias in large language models (LLMs) can persist despite instructions to ignore presentation order or prompts that elicit reasoning. Recent efforts to reproduce Jev-style System One behavior have produced a growing family of models that predict probabilities directly over supplied candidates. items.title: Pretraining Knows What, Simulation Teaches How: Compositional Generalization in a Sim-Trained Robot Agent
items.summary: A robot policy needs to understand what a task is asking for in a scene, and how to move the robot to accomplish that task. To achieve these two skills, we introduce Zero-real Agent Policy (ZAP), a recipe that teaches a small off-the-shelf vision-language model to control a robot via a simple tool harness. We use a pretrained 27B parameter model to bootstrap world understanding and reasoning…

items.title: Does VGGT Know What It Does Not Know?
items.summary: Feed-forward 3D reconstruction models such as VGGT regress cameras and geometry in a single forward pass, but they report no uncertainty for the camera poses they predict: an incorrect relative pose looks no different from a correct one. We ask whether the frozen model nonetheless knows when its pose is wrong. On HardMatch, a benchmark of 1,000 deliberately difficult image pairs on which VGGT…

items.title: Learning When to Commit: Schedule Distillation for Fast Diffusion Language Models
items.summary: Diffusion large language models (dLLMs) can generate multiple tokens in parallel, but often require many decoding rounds to complete a response. Efficient generation depends not only on which tokens are easy to predict, but also on how committing to them helps predict the remaining positions. A highly predictable token may provide little useful context, while revealing a less predictable token…

items.title: Game theory of academic effort and hiring in the age of AI
items.summary: Many academic disciplines (in particular, mathematics and the theoretical sciences) face difficult questions about how to adapt their practices to the rise of highly capable artificial intelligence (AI). items.title: FOCUS: Active Critic Learning for Long-Horizon Language Model Agents
items.summary: Sparse outcome rewards make it difficult for long-horizon language-model agents to assign credit to earlier actions. Learned critics provide value estimates for intermediate states, but these estimates can be inaccurate, while estimating intermediate values with repetitive continuation samples from points within a trajectory incurs substantial costs. To mitigate these issues, we introduce FOCUS…

items.title: Quantifying Claim Smoothing by LLM Research Agents
items.summary: Deep research, or any use of large language models (LLMs) to read a large document collection and produce insights, requires synthesizing information from different sources. In this work, we find that LLMs produce long-form research reports that read as confident syntheses but which fail to accurately reflect the underlying documents. We call this failure smoothing. items.title: Selective Tie Learning: Mitigating Spurious Correlations in Preference Optimization
items.summary: Preference optimization can learn spurious correlations, and augmenting the preference data with ties (equally preferred responses) can reduce spurious reliance. However, ties differ in their corrective effect, making their selection for augmentation important.
